segments.text: Louise, come in. Good to see you. Last time, you were telling me about the sourdough you had just started. Did it survive?
It did survive, actually. It lives in the fridge now, and I feed it every Sunday. The bread is finally getting a proper crust, so I am quite proud of myself.
That sounds like real progress. So, what brings you in today?
It is my knee. I keep getting pain behind my right kneecap, and it keeps coming back. It is not there all the time, which is partly why I put off calling you.
Tell me more about that. When you say it comes back, does it settle in between?
Yes, exactly. It comes and goes. Some days, I barely notice it, and then it turns up again behind the kneecap. That on-and-off pattern is what made me want it looked at.
I understand.
And it is...
Is specifically the right knee?
The right one, yes. The left has never bothered me at all. It is always right behind the kneecap, sort of underneath it, if that makes sense.
It does. Thank you for describing it so clearly.
I keep wondering whether I did something to it. Honestly, I cannot point to a single moment where it started. It just crept in.
That happens more often than people expect.
Right. So, what do you think is going on in there?
From what you described...
From what you described, I suspect a condition called chondromalacia patelli. That is, softening or wear of the cartilage on the underside of the kneecap.
Chondromalacia. That is a mouthful. So, the cartilage under the kneecap is the problem?
That is the area we are talking about, yes. I want to be clear that this is a clinical suspicion at this stage, not something confirmed.
Okay, so you are not certain yet. I appreciate you saying that plainly.
I would rather know where we stand than be told everything is fine.
I would rather be straight with you, too. That is why I do not want to leave it at a suspicion.
So, there is a next step?
There is. I am going to refer you for an arthroscopy. That is a keyhole procedure where a small camera is used to look inside the joint.
A camera inside the knee. Well, that sounds more involved than I expected when I walked in here.
I know it sounds like a lot the first time you hear it. It is the step that lets us actually see the surface behind your kneecap.
That does make sense. I suppose guessing about it forever would be worse. And I have been guessing for a while now.
You have. Let us get you a proper look instead.
Can I ask something completely unrelated? Are those plants on the windowsill yours? They look far healthier than anything I own.
They are mine.
And the secret is that I mostly leave them alone.
That is a relief to hear. I keep watering mine into an early grave. Maybe benign neglect is the answer for my kitchen windowsill as well.
It has worked in here so far. Now, back to the knee.
Yes, of course. Sorry, I do wander.
Not at all. I will send the referral for the arthroscopy, and you will be contacted about an appointment.
Good. So, I wait to hear from them.
Yes.
Rather than chasing it myself.
That is right. The referral goes from here.
Understood. I will keep an eye out for the letter then. It is good to have a plan after all this wandering.
I think so too. We will talk again once you have been seen, Louise.
Thank you. And I will bring you a loaf if the sourdough behaves itself.
